honesty_notice: Every claim below was produced by running the named command. Numbers were read off disk, not recalled. Claims that were NOT measured say so.

spec_source.numbering_caveat: The file has 29273 CRLF and 166 BARE CR. Python text-mode (universal newlines) numbering runs ~112-166 lines HIGHER than Read-tool numbering for the same content. All citations use Read-tool numbering, which matches the pinned ranges. A citation copied from a `grep` run in text mode will be off by ~112 lines in this region.

commands.lint: python -m ruff check platform/lib/councilspec/   (run from the REPO ROOT; a relative path from platform/lib makes ruff report a path error that reads like a lint failure)

claims.schema_is_valid_2020_12: CONFIRMED - jsonschema 4.25.1 validator_for() resolves Draft202012Validator and check_schema() passes (test_schema_is_a_valid_draft_2020_12_schema).
claims.six_required_examples_validate: CONFIRMED - all 6 spec stopping expressions from lines 10937-10942 are encoded as full CouncilSpec instances under examples/valid/ and every one reports 0 schema errors and 0 semantic errors.
claims.must_fail_instance_rejected: CONFIRMED - invalid/N1-typed-leaf-violation.councilspec.json (`unanimity >= 0.95`, a boolean metric with a numeric operator) is rejected by the SCHEMA: "$['stopping']['expression']: ... is not valid under any of the given schemas". CLI exits 1 with FAILED:councilspec-validate.
claims.leaf_is_typed_not_merely_shaped: CONFIRMED - the metric-name enum sets for the numeric/boolean/enum leaf branches are disjoint (asserted), so the oneOf can match at most one branch and a domain/operator/value mismatch has nowhere to land.
claims.expression_string_roundtrip: CONFIRMED AT TREE LEVEL ONLY - parse(unparse(tree)) == tree for all six. Byte-level text round-trip is explicitly NOT claimed and a test asserts it is FALSE (0.90 normalises to 0.9).
claims.expression_evaluator_executes: CONFIRMED - each of the six evaluates True on its satisfying snapshot and False on its non-satisfying snapshot (both-states control). A missing metric raises MissingMetricError rather than reading as false; a wrongly-typed snapshot value raises MetricTypeError.
claims.any_all_sugar: CONFIRMED - ANY[a, b] / ALL[a, b] (the surface form used by the preset catalogue and named at spec line 10760) parse to the same trees as `a OR b` / `a AND b`. Sugar is INPUT ONLY; unparse always emits the AND/OR form.
claims.weighted_stopping_logic: CONFIRMED - the weighted node (clauses with weights plus a threshold) is schema-typed, exercised by E6 subcouncil A, and unit-tested at the threshold boundary (0.7 sum vs 0.7 threshold fires).
claims.recursion_nested_and_council_of_councils: CONFIRMED - topology.subcouncils items are `$ref: '#'`; a defect planted in E6's SECOND subcouncil fails the PARENT, at both the schema layer and the semantic layer (path reported as $.topology.subcouncils[1]...).
claims.semantic_rules_enforced: CONFIRMED - 12 rules; 5 distinct rules (SEM-001/002/007/008/011) are each proven to fire by a dedicated fixture, and SEM-005/006/009/012 by unit tests. A clean spec produces ZERO findings (detector control, test_a_healthy_spec_produces_no_findings_at_all).
claims.mutation_control_ran: CONFIRMED - every invalid fixture is generated as exactly ONE mutation of a named PASSING base (make_negatives.py); tests assert the base still validates, that the on-disk fixture matches the declared mutation byte-for-byte, and that no fixture changed more than its declared top-level key.
claims.runner_is_not_vacuous: CONFIRMED - four both-states tests break a copy of the examples tree (a positive made invalid, a negative repaired, an unlisted file added, a manifest file deleted) and the runner goes RED in all four.
claims.cross_implementation_agreement: CONFIRMED - the independently authored sibling parser platform/lib/wfdsl/expr.py agrees with this one on all 6 spec expressions in both states (agree=6 disagree=0 errored=0).
claims.prior_design_section_coverage: PARTIAL - 8 of the prior 13 section NAMES in 11-COUNCIL-SPECIFICATION.schema.json are absent as top-level keys here (artifacts, charter, engagement, evidence, integrity, meta, roles are RENAMED/nested; `execution` has NO counterpart). Field-NAME overlap is only 44/199 (22%), but that probe counts property names only and therefore under-counts semantics that this schema expresses as enum members instead of fields. A field-by-field semantic reconciliation was NOT performed.
claims.presets_validate_unchanged: REFUTED AS A REQUIREMENT - 0 of the 72 preset rows in 12-COUNCIL-PROTOCOLS-AND-PRESETS.json validate against this schema, AND 0 of 72 validate against the prior 11-COUNCIL-SPECIFICATION.schema.json either. Doc 12 states in its own `schema_relationship` field that NO schema governs it and that it is a CATALOGUE. The rows carry compact string dials ("stopping": "ANY[rounds>=1, chair_confident]", "budgets": "wall<=90s tokens<=8k tools<=4"), so requiring them to validate as CouncilSpec instances is a category error. WORK-UNIT-CATALOG IMP-3's falsifiable question is therefore UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN for any CouncilSpec schema; the missing contract is a preset-row schema plus a row-to-CouncilSpec compiler.
claims.preset_metric_vocabulary: NOT-CHECKED as satisfiable - preset rows reference metric names outside this registry (`rounds`, `chair_confident`). Settling experiment: write the preset-row compiler and either add an alias map (rounds -> rounds_elapsed) or extend the registry, then re-run this probe over all 72 rows.
claims.48_protocol_blueprints_and_64_presets: NOT-CHECKED - out of scope for this unit. This unit ships the SCHEMA that can express them (25 preset names, 20 stage kinds, 11 topologies); it does not ship 48 blueprint instances or 64 editable preset files.
claims.receipt_schema_reference: UNRESOLVED BY DESIGN - platform/schema/receipt.schema.json now EXISTS (sibling unit), while every output_schema in command-center/WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json still points at command-center/schema/receipt.schema.json, which does NOT. outputs.receipt_schema is therefore a documented reference string, not a resolved $ref.

known_gaps: No `execution` section (runner, concurrency, heartbeat, config hash, provenance) - the one prior-design section with no counterpart here.
The 21 top-level sections do not use the prior design's 13 section names; a reconciliation decision is owed (rename this schema, or record the mapping as normative).

$id conventions across the 8 platform/schema/*.schema.json files are split two ways, measured 2026-08-09: 6 use https://schema.ast-integrate.local/<name>/<ver> (work-unit x4, workflow-dsl, and councilspec after aligning it to the majority) and 2 use https://ast-integrate.invalid/platform/schema/<file> (receipt, completion-predicate-result). Neither is wrong on its own - .invalid is the RFC-2606 reserved choice, .local is mDNS - but one convention should be picked before anything resolves a $ref across contracts.
coverage: MEASURED: schema validity, all six required examples, the must-fail instance, typed-leaf enforcement, tree round-trip, both-states evaluation, recursion, 12 semantic rules, fixture-mutation integrity, runner non-vacuity, cross-implementation agreement, prior-design section coverage, and preset validity. NOT MEASURED: field-by-field semantic reconciliation against the prior schema, preset-row compilation, and the 48-blueprint / 64-preset population.
